title: An enemy brain
description:
Write the state machine of lesson 4.04 and the field-of-view test:

```cpp
struct Vector2 { float x, y; };

bool inView(Vector2 pos, Vector2 facing, Vector2 target, float range, float halfAngleDegrees);

enum class State { Patrol, Alert, Chase, Attack, Return, Hurt };
struct Senses { bool seesPlayer; float distance; bool attackFinished; bool atPatrolRoute; bool wasHit; };
struct Brain { State state{ State::Patrol }; float timer{ 0 }; float unseen{ 0 }; };

void think(Brain& b, const Senses& s, float dt);
std::string name(State s);   // "Patrol", "Alert", ...
```

**inView**: the target is within `range` (inclusive) and within `halfAngleDegrees` of the facing direction (`facing` has length 1). A target exactly at `pos` is in view.

**think**: first `timer += dt`. A hit (`wasHit`) always enters **Hurt**, from any state, even Hurt itself. Otherwise, by state:

| State | Changes to |
|---|---|
| Patrol | Alert if it sees the player |
| Alert | Chase once `timer >= 0.3` (the reaction time) |
| Chase | Attack if `distance < 24`; otherwise counts `unseen` up by `dt` while not seeing the player (back to 0 when seeing them) and goes to Return when `unseen >= 3` |
| Attack | Chase when `attackFinished` |
| Return | Chase if it sees the player; Patrol when `atPatrolRoute` |
| Hurt | Chase once `timer >= 0.3` |

Entering a state sets `timer` and `unseen` to 0. At most one change happens per call.
hints: Write a small `enter` helper that sets the state and resets both timers, and use it for every change.
